definition: A use-sensitive account attends to the rule-governed inferential and practical role of an expression in a specified activity when determining competent uses. Identifying a named object need not exhaust that role. Use here is not raw frequency, unanimous endorsement, an exhaustive list of sentence-truth values or a stipulation that nothing refers.
note: Stipulative analyst sense for the OPEN position in #1090; attribution DEFERRED. Some expressions/practices only, not a universal meaning identity. Existing REFERENCE-ANCHOR-BOUNDARY concerns the narrower full first-order truth/inference profile; it does not prove this philosophical position or eliminate its structuralist rival. See docs/wittgenstein.md.
